content.text: How should I analyze a due process question?

Due process analysis has two branches: (1) PROCEDURAL due process - when government deprives someone of life, liberty, or property, what process is due? Apply Mathews v. Eldridge balancing: private interest affected, risk of erroneous deprivation, government's interest. Required procedures typically include notice, opportunity to be heard, and neutral decision-maker. (2) SUBSTANTIVE due process - whether government can take the action at all. For fundamental rights (marriage, procreation, family, privacy), apply strict scrutiny. For non-fundamental rights (economic), apply rational basis. Remember: 5th Amendment applies to federal government, 14th Amendment incorporates against states.
Explain the Commerce Clause and its limits

The Commerce Clause (Art. I, §8) grants Congress power to regulate: (1) Channels of interstate commerce (highways, waterways, internet), (2) Instrumentalities of interstate commerce (trucks, planes, persons/things in commerce), (3) Activities substantially affecting interstate commerce. After Lopez/Morrison, purely local, non-economic activity may be beyond Congress's reach. The Dormant Commerce Clause limits state regulation: states cannot discriminate against or unduly burden interstate commerce. Exceptions: Congressional authorization, market participant doctrine (state as buyer/seller), and traditional government functions. For bar exam, also know the 10th Amendment anti-commandeering principle: Congress cannot compel states to enact or enforce federal programs.
